data.title: Fed policymakers concerned about financial system risks, minutes show
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Financial stability risks tied to aggressive artificial intelligence investment and elevated asset prices are on the US central bank's radar, the minutes from the Federal Reserve's policy meeting last month showed on Wednesday.

The concern was raised as part of a broad review of financial risks by Fed policymakers and central bank staff at the October 27-28 policy meeting. That gathering saw officials hold interest rates steady despite ongoing worries about high and persistent levels of inflation. However, "almost all" policymakers agreed that further hikes would be needed if the economy evolved as they expected, the minutes showed. 

"The staff judged that current vulnerabilities could amplify shocks somewhat more than usual, with elevated asset valuations and leverage at hedge funds representing the most salient vulnerabilities, while strong bank and household balance sheets provided an important buffer against more severe outcomes," the minutes said.

Policymakers expressed concern that huge levels of investment in AI technology could lead to trouble and create broader problems for both the financial system and economy.

"Almost all participants commented on risks associated with a scenario in which the returns on AI investment turned out to be disappointing to investors," the minutes said. "Most participants observed that AI-related debt had grown rapidly and that much of this growth had taken place through complex and opaque financing structures," while "a few" of the unnamed Fed officials were concerned that AI exposure was being concentrated in a "small number" of companies.

Fed officials also cast an anxious eye toward hedge funds.

"Most participants highlighted hedge fund leverage or limited dealer intermediation capacity as potential channels of amplification during periods of market stress," the minutes said.

Fed staff described the financial system as "resilient," with banks having ample access to cash, according to the minutes. But some policymakers worried that "banking system vulnerabilities could emerge rapidly even after seemingly reassuring initial assessments."

Some were also worried the Fed's data on the banking system may miss the full range of exposure some financial firms have.

BUILDING RESILIENCE

Financial markets have been under stress in recent weeks amid questions about the future of AI and how the buildout of the technology has increasingly come to rely on debt. Past periods of financial trouble have been frequently associated with excessive borrowing, and some of those crises have driven the Fed to intervene to stabilize markets.

The latest minutes also showed Fed officials weighing how they can respond to future troubles.

"A few" policymakers mulled boosting banks' capital levels while some also said it is important to better prepare banks to use the Fed's emergency lending discount window facility, which is something officials have been working on for some time.

In addition, "a few" policymakers considered a novel strategy in which the Fed would set up a dedicated method of asset-buying that would explicitly target financial stability concerns.

The Fed is weighing the future of how it uses its balance sheet as a policy tool. Fed holdings have swollen massively over the last two decades due to huge bond purchases during the 2008 global financial crisis and the COVID-19 pandemic.

The pandemic experience has loomed particularly large because bond-buying that began in March 2020 started out as a stabilization tool that morphed into outright stimulus.

Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack is among those who would like to see a more clearly defined system for buying bonds that would also entail a strategy to sell them when a crisis has passed. Hammack said earlier this week that any program "should also be temporary, and holdings should be sold in a timely way once market financial stability is restored." 

The minutes noted that "several" policymakers cautioned that monetary policy is not the right tool to deal with market trouble. But the large role now played by AI and technology investment in driving economic growth might complicate that view if large-scale problems emerged.

(Reporting by Michael S. Derby; Editing by Paul Simao)

data.title: KSAT, ESA, and INTA Collaborate to Establish KSAT's Lunar Communications Infrastructure in Spain to Strengthen KSAT Lunar Network
data.description:
TROMSØ, Norway and CEBREROS, Spain, Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Kongsberg Satellite Services (KSAT), the European Space Agency (ESA), and Instituto Nacional de Técnica Aeroespacial (INTA) have entered into a collaboration aimed at strengthening communications capabilities for future lunar missions through closer cooperation between institutional and commercial partners. As part of the collaboration, KSAT will establish a lunar communications network site in the vicinity of ESA's ground station in Cebreros, Spain, drawing on ESA and INTA Infrastructure services and operational capabilities.

The collaboration will support the establishment of KSAT's 20-meter-class antenna and dedicated lunar communications capabilities at Cebreros. Together with KSAT's Western Australian and Arizona sites, the Cebreros site will become a key European element for the KSAT Lunar network, providing critical global coverage and high-availability communications services that enable mission success. The collaboration will also foster European participation in lunar exploration, supporting the development of a commercially available connectivity services to deep space and cislunar space.

"This collaboration represents another important milestone in the development of the global communications infrastructure needed to support sustained lunar exploration," said Marte Indregard, Chief Executive Officer at Kongsberg Satellite Services. "By working with ESA and INTA at the strategically located Cebreros site, we are expanding the reach and resilience of our Lunar Network while strengthening Europe's capacity in lunar exploration and discovery."

"ESA is committed to fostering partnerships that drive the development of new communications capabilities and strengthen Europe's role in future lunar operations," said Octave Procope-Mamert, Head of the Ground Operations division at the European Space Agency/ESOC. "By bringing together ESA's expertise in deep space communications and operations with the capabilities of KSAT and INTA, this collaboration marks an important step towards delivering robust and interoperable solutions. It will enhance the versatility and scalability of the ESTRACK augmented network by enabling access to complementary commercial capabilities, helping meet the evolving demands of the next generation of lunar missions."

"This initiative highlights the value of combining national infrastructure, international cooperation, and commercial innovation," stated Cecilio Caballero, a representative of the Instituto Nacional de Técnica Aeroespacial (INTA). "The Cebreros facilities enjoy a privileged location for supporting the next generation of exploration missions, and for INTA contributing to the definition and provision of the site for this important effort."

With sites strategically distributed across three continents, KSAT's lunar network will extend the company's existing global ground-station capabilities, including more than 300 satellite communications antennas worldwide, into cislunar space.

About KSAT
Kongsberg Satellite Services (KSAT) is a global provider of ground network services, Earth observation services and government programs. Headquartered in Tromsø, Norway, and co-owned by Kongsberg Defense & Aerospace and Space Norway, KSAT operates the world's largest commercial satellite ground station network, including sites in Svalbard and Antarctica, and delivers mission-critical infrastructure for government, civil and commercial space customers worldwide.

About ESA
The European Space Agency (ESA) is Europe's gateway to space.
ESA is an intergovernmental organization, created in 1975, with the mission to shape the development of Europe's space capability and ensure that investment in space delivers benefits to the citizens of Europe and the world.
By coordinating the financial and intellectual resources of its members, ESA can undertake programmes and activities far beyond the scope of any single European country. It is working in particular with the EU on implementing the Galileo and Copernicus programmes as well as with Eumetsat for the development of meteorological missions.
Learn more about ESA at www.esa.int.

About INTA
The Instituto Nacional de Técnica Aeroespacial (INTA), created in 1942, is the Spanish Public Research Organisation that operates under the Spanish Ministry of Defence.
INTA participates in international space programs and develops dual-use technology for scientific and technological missions in the fields of aeronautics, space, naval hydrodynamics, security, and defence.
Learn more about INTA at www.inta.es.

* Dollar index hits fresh 19-month high

* Oil prices slide on larger-than-expected inventories

By Rodrigo Campos

NEW YORK/LONDON, Nov 18 (Reuters) - A gauge of global stocks fell in choppy trading on Wednesday after Nvidia's ( NVDA ) quarterly results and ahead of Anthropic's market debut, while the dollar's strength also weighed on sentiment.

The dollar strengthened to a fresh 19-month high after US Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller told CNBC the central bank needs to either approve a half-point interest rate hike at its December meeting or communicate a faster pace of hikes in 2027.

Mining stocks dragged European shares lower, while Nvidia's ( NVDA ) results initially helped Asian shares, with Korea's Kospi up 2% overnight. But the Nvidia ( NVDA ) rally fizzled and the stock was down 2.4% after rising as much as 2.7%.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board dismissed the idea of rehiring former CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned last week. The company forecast sales ahead of Wall Street targets on Tuesday.

"The central question Nvidia ( NVDA ) faces is not related to this earnings report ... it's more about what the company may look like in 3-5 years without a visionary leader like Jensen and as competition from other chipmakers takes shape," said Jay Peters, portfolio manager at NewEdge Wealth.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.84% to 50,334.82, the S&P 500 eased 0.07% to 7,335.43 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.46% to 24,439.22.

MSCI's gauge of global stocks fell 0.34% to 1,075.82 and the pan-European STOXX 600 index dropped 1.03%. Emerging market stocks eased 0.13% and Japan's Nikkei rose 0.28%.

The next health check on the AI industry will come as Anthropic prepares to price its shares on Wednesday ahead of its market debut.

DOLLAR UP, OIL DOWN

In currencies, the dollar strengthened as Waller's comments and recent economic data cemented expectations for an interest rate hike next month.

"The Federal Reserve seems at the moment to be very determined to hike interest rates and maybe even aggressively do so," said Juan Perez, senior director of trading at Monex USA in Washington. "That's the belief right now that's carrying the US dollar."

The dollar index rose 0.19% to 103.81, with the euro down 0.24% at $1.0971.

In commodities markets, crude prices fell after US crude and fuel inventories rose more than expected, adding to expectations of a supply surplus.

US crude fell 4.39% to $82.23 a barrel and Brent dropped to $90.93 per barrel, down 2.37%.

Spot gold fell 2.86% to $3,739.66 an ounce and spot silver lost 4.72% to $45.16 an ounce. Copper declined 4.69% to $12,606.00 a ton.

US Treasury yields were slightly lower as oil prices dropped, dragging inflation expectations lower.

data.title: Grand Theft Auto VI draws rave reviews as gamers enter Vice City
data.description:
By Aditya Soni and Cordelia Hsu

SYDNEY, Nov 19 (Reuters) - After 13 years and an estimated $1 billion or more in production costs, "Grand Theft Auto VI" began rolling out across the globe on Thursday, gaining rapturous early reviews for the most anticipated video game release in history.

The game, which could bring in billions of dollars for its developer, Take-Two Interactive studio Rockstar Games, raced to the top of Metacritic's all-time gaming leaderboard with a score of 99, a mark matched by only one other title, Nintendo's 1998 classic "The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time".

"GTA VI is popping off, it is the best game that's ever been made and we're only 20 minutes deep," said 33-year-old Sydney gamer Asif Mir as he started to play and livestream in his gaming room just after midnight.

"I cannot wait to go 12 hours, 10 hours until tomorrow morning. I ain't getting any sleep. Let's go, man!"

The game went online as midnight struck in New Zealand, with launches worldwide set to follow the clock through Thursday. Miami, the inspiration for the game's setting, will be one of the last places to get in on the action.

Millions of players have already downloaded the game to their consoles, with many expected to take time off work - or call in sick - to play the latest installment in a franchise that since its 1997 debut has become one of the best-selling video game series of all time.

"It's the Star Wars of this generation, right?" said Joost van Dreunen, adjunct professor at NYU Stern School of Business.

"It's a synchronized, shared event. So millions of people will all want to be there the first couple of days, the first few weeks of experiencing it as it goes live."

Strong initial reviews of the game - available on Sony's ( SONY ) PlayStation 5 and Microsoft's ( MSFT ) Xbox Series X and ​S consoles - helped push up Take-Two Interactive's US shares by over 8% in early trading.

'TRULY ASTONISHING': GAME GETS STRONG USER REVIEWS

The original "Grand Theft Auto" looks basic by today's standards and its missions - stealing cars and carrying out jobs for ​crime syndicates - angered politicians and parents, even as they delighted gamers.

But as the series progressed it got increasingly sophisticated, mixing its trademark crime, driving and morally dubious missions with activities ranging from parachute jumps to cinema visits and radio stations satirizing US culture.

"Grand Theft Auto V", released in 2013, was set in the fictional Los Santos, a stand-in for Los Angeles. The action now moves to Vice City, a fictional version of Miami, in the state of Leonida, the game's take on Florida.

Play will switch between two leading characters, Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval. They are partners in crime and romantically involved - just how romantically will be up to the player. There will be nightclubs, gun stores, scuba diving and a zoo. But much remains to be revealed.

GTA VI could prove less provocative than its predecessors, said Tore Olsson, a professor at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville, who teaches a course on US history since 1980 through the GTA games. The game sits more within mainstream culture now and its promotional materials suggest it will reward more ethical play styles, he said.

"There's no doubt that Jason and Lucia of VI will be criminals, and they'll be regularly breaking the law. But I don't think the new game will require players to enact wanton slaughter, and it may indeed penalize those who choose to play that way," said Olsson.

Having Lucia as one of the two lead characters should help address complaints about a lack of playable female characters in previous iterations of GTA. Women will be an estimated 4 out of 10 GTA VI players in the US, according to a Bain survey.

Initial sales were strong, with analytics firm Sensor Tower estimating some 17 million copies sold for more than $1.65 billion as of Wednesday.

With so much anticipation, the risk of disappointment is high. Play that is perceived as too easy or too hard, an unsatisfying storyline, or significant bugs and glitches at launch can all affect a game's reputation and future sales.

But early signs were positive.

Entertainment website GamesRadar+ said Rockstar had built a world of "truly astonishing scale, scope, and quality". Video game website Eurogamer Poland cited some dips in performance, but said those did "little to dull the shine of one of the best and most engrossing games of this generation".

'PROBABLY THE GREATEST GAME OF ALL TIME'

With the main part of the game estimated to take around 50 hours to complete, full reactions were not available immediately. But some fans have said they will stay up all night and/or take the day off work to dive straight in.

"(When) 'Grand Theft Auto V' came out I was a child, and so the anticipation is crazy," said Brayden Whaley, a 23-year-old content creator from Los Angeles.

"For me personally, I'm going to enter flow state and what that means is basically I'm going to complete the entire game and not get off of it until I complete it."

Luke Maxwell, a 27-year-old father of two who works in sales on Australia's Gold Coast, said he had booked time off from work so he could get stuck in straightaway: "I've already told the whole family, don't bother me, don't talk to me."

Back in Sydney, Mir said the long wait had been worth it.

"I've waited 13 years, man, 13 years! (It's) probably the greatest game of all time."

(Additional reporting by Rosalba O'Brien in New York, Matt Silverstein in Los Angeles, Adrianna Ebert in Gdansk and Christine Chen in Sydney; Writing by Rosalba O'Brien and Adam Jourdan; Editing by Daniel Wallis, Kate Mayberry, Mark Potter and Catherine Evans)

data.title: Healthcare AI Shakeout: Health Systems Plan to Cut AI Vendors Nearly in Half by 2028, Black Book Finds
data.description:
NEW YORK CITY, NY / ACCESS Newswire / November 18, 2026 / Healthcare artificial intelligence is approaching a major market consolidation as health systems prepare to eliminate nearly half their standalone AI vendors by 2028, according to new independent research from Black Book Market Research.

The study, AI Vendor Survival Odds 2027-2028, surveyed 412 verified healthcare AI buyers across six technology categories and 14 product segments, revealing a growing disconnect between AI investment, realized financial returns and vendor staying power.

Five Findings Reshaping Healthcare AI

  • 44% fewer AI vendors: Health systems plan to reduce their median standalone AI vendor count from nine today to five by 2028. Larger AI portfolios face even steeper consolidation, declining from 17 to eight among top-quartile systems.
  • 41% of promised ROI realized: Buyers report achieving a median of just 41% of the returns promised at sale. Autonomous coding leads at 66%, while policy and checklist governance tools trail at 18%.
  • Ambient AI faces a reckoning: Buyers expect only three of today's 11 major ambient documentation vendors to remain independent by 2028.
  • EHR platforms threaten standalone AI: 63% of Epic-based health systems plan to replace at least one standalone AI tool with native EHR capabilities, versus 34% of organizations using other EHRs.
  • Contracts expose buyers to consolidation risk: 71% of AI contracts lack change-of-control termination rights, while 77% lack exit rights if the EHR delivers equivalent native functionality.

The Next AI Winners May Not Be Today's Fastest-Growing Vendors

"Healthcare AI is entering a renewal-driven shakeout, not an innovation slowdown. The existential threat to many AI companies isn't another startup with a better algorithm. It's an incumbent EHR delivering comparable functionality inside an existing contract, while the CFO questions whether the original investment ever paid for itself," said Doug Brown, Founder of Black Book.

"For investors, customer acquisition and deployment counts are increasingly inadequate measures of enterprise value. A vendor can have enthusiastic users, impressive growth and substantial funding yet still be economically replaceable. The next generation of winners will be defined by defensible workflow integration, independently demonstrable outcomes and the ability to survive the customer's next renewal decision."

Which AI Categories Appear Most Resilient?

Imaging and pathology AI leads Black Book's comparative Survival Index at 73 out of 100, followed by patient communications and AI contact centers at 71.

Ambient clinical documentation ranks lowest at 56, reflecting greater exposure to native EHR replacement.

Black Book also identifies a consequential governance gap: 61% of board respondents believe their AI contracts protect them in an acquisition, compared with just 24% of CIOs.

The implication: Healthcare AI consolidation may be driven as much by purchasing economics, contractual exposure and platform absorption as by technological performance.

data.title: Anthropic IPO to mint thousands of millionaires
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Anthropic's initial public offering is poised to create thousands of paper millionaires among current and former employees, in what could rank among the largest employee wealth windfalls in Silicon Valley history.  

The offering is expected to unleash a wave of new wealth across the AI sector, rewarding everyone from early researchers and engineers to administrative staff who received stock grants as the Claude maker raced from startup to one of the world's most valuable companies.

The IPO filing shows the amount of wealth embedded in employee stock awards, but not how that wealth is distributed among workers. As a result, outside estimates vary widely.

Hill, a San Francisco marketplace for private-company shares, estimates 598 non-founder employees will hold at least $100 million in equity after the initial public offering, which is slated to open on the Nasdaq on Thursday at $70 to $78 a share, valuing the firm at up to $1.4 trillion. The final pricing should be decided on Wednesday night.

Private-markets research firm Sacra estimates that roughly 2,800 current and former Anthropic employees could hold at least $1 million of pretax vested equity at a $1.35 trillion valuation, the middle of the price range. 

The firms say their estimates are model-based and use public information. Reuters could not independently verify the estimates, which reflect factors including vesting periods, exercises, tender transactions, option awards, restricted stock units, award timing, headcount and employee retention rates. The filing does not disclose sums due individuals.

But the wealth potentially shared by employees is vast.  Anthropic option holders were sitting on $119 billion of paper gains as of September 30, at a weighted average exercise price of $2.91 per share, the company disclosed. About $73 billion of that amount had vested through service and could be exercised immediately. 

Anthropic did not respond to a comment request on the estimates.

"The idea of equity appreciating to an amount that is life-changing is something that people strive for," Hill CEO Andrew Benson said. "It doesn't get better than this."

EQUITY AT ENTRY LEVEL

Workers who joined the firm when it started five years ago -  even in administrative positions and entry-level jobs - could be sitting on life-changing wealth, reflecting their holdings of stock options that carry exercise prices of less than $1. 

Options granted through 2023 and still outstanding at the end of that year carried an average exercise price of 52 cents, the filing shows. 

At SpaceX, which was founded in 2002 and went  public in June in a record-busting IPO, many of the employees who became millionaires had worked there for more than a decade.   

"Early employees who started in a very junior role should have actually a better financial outcome than somebody who joined in a very senior role right before the IPO," Benson said, referring to Anthropic.

Non-founder Anthropic employees can sell up to 10% of their holdings on the first trading day, and up to another 35% after fiscal 2026 earnings.

EARLY HIRES REAP REWARDS

Founded in 2021, the Claude maker expanded its workforce rapidly alongside the AI boom, growing to about 5,300 employees as of September 30 from roughly 940 at the end of 2024. As it hired aggressively, the company used stock-based compensation as a key recruiting tool.

A May 2024 job posting for an administrative business partner role shows how the benefits of Anthropic's stock awards extended beyond AI researchers and engineers. 

The position, which involved scheduling and managing calendars for company leaders, coordinating conference logistics and handling expense claims and reimbursements, paid an annual salary of $140,000 to $190,000. 

The posting added that equity would be "a major component of the total compensation" beyond the salary, indicating that administrative and support staff were also eligible for stock awards alongside cash pay.

That year, Anthropic said it granted employees options at an average exercise price of $1.30 per share.

"And as we know from several anecdotes after the SpaceX IPO, this is often enough to help people down the organization chart do quite well in IPO," said Marcelo Ballve, head of research at Sacra.

Anthropic granted CFO Krishna Rao 14 million stock options in 2024, also with a $1.30 exercise price, according to the filing. At the IPO price range, those options would carry roughly $1 billion in gross intrinsic value, before exercise costs and taxes.

Ballve said that equity awards for administrative, support and entry-level roles are not uncommon at venture capital-backed companies. Historically, though, many companies phased out equity grants at hiring for these roles as they scaled up and salaries became more competitive, moving to performance- and tenure-based grants instead.

After Anthropic goes public, the company will likely reserve upfront equity grants solely for recruiting top talent, he said.

(Reporting by Sabrina Valle in New York; Editing by Colin Barr and Matthew Lewis)

data.title: Nvidia retreats as strong outlook fails to dispel uncertainty
data.description:
By Anhata Rooprai and Shashwat Chauhan

Nov 18 (Reuters) - Nvidia ( NVDA ) shares dipped on Wednesday, with analysts more optimistic about future earnings while also more cautious about future stock gains following the AI chip giant's blockbuster forecast and uncertainty caused by CEO Jensen Huang's departure last week.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) fell 2.8%, increasing its loss to 36% from its October 6 record-high close, with much of that drop related to Huang's resignation after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang and two with Nvidia ( NVDA ) employees.

Following Nvidia's ( NVDA ) strong report and outlook, the average analyst estimate for its adjusted net income in its next fiscal year has climbed to $393 billion from $380 billion before Tuesday's late-day report, according to LSEG data.

At the same time, the average analyst price target has dipped to $251.74 from $265.70 on Monday. The stock was last at $152.

The higher earnings estimates and lower price targets show analysts believe Nvidia's ( NVDA ) business remains strong but are applying a more cautious valuation, reflecting risks around the CEO transition and AI spending.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 has shed around $2 trillion in market value so far in November, as investors reassessed lofty AI valuations alongside concerns over China, data center spending and tighter regulation.

"We believe yesterday's results have stabilized sentiment and put a floor under the recent AI selloff, but they have postponed rather than permanently cured investor anxiety," said Neil Shah, vice president of research at Counterpoint.

The next test of the AI trade will come when Anthropic prices its initial public offering later on Wednesday, which could value the frontier lab at up to $1.4 trillion.

Also weighing on shares of Nvidia ( NVDA ) and other AI companies, the Wall Street Journal reported that the US Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating the chipmaker.

The AI trade has also been tested since the Democrats' sweeping midterm wins stoked fears of tougher regulation of data center buildouts, sending the tech-heavy Nasdaq into correction territory earlier this month.

BOARD SAYS NO TO HUANG

Nvidia ( NVDA ) Chairman Harvey Jones ruled out reinstating Huang despite his offer to return. Heidrick & Struggles is leading the search for a permanent CEO among both internal and external candidates.

The stock might struggle to climb further until the company names a permanent CEO and the new leadership shows it can deliver planned products, HSBC analysts said.

Interim CEO Colette Kress has said it was "business as usual," citing customer and supplier support. Nvidia's ( NVDA ) forecast offered evidence that the upheaval has not delayed its product roadmap or weakened demand.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) fourth-quarter revenue forecast beat analysts' estimates, while the company also raised its fiscal 2028 revenue growth outlook to about 75%, saying demand continued to exceed supply.

Third-quarter revenue more than doubled to $115.84 billion, marking a 17th consecutive estimate beat, according to LSEG data.

Adjusted gross margin reached 74.9%. Nvidia ( NVDA ) expects it to bottom between 71% and 72% this quarter as higher supply costs bite, before recovering to between 72% and 73% in fiscal 2028.

"Strong earnings have bought management time," Saxo strategist Charu Chanana said.

CHINA DISAPPEARS FROM OUTLOOK

China contributed $2.4 billion in licensed Hopper data center sales during the quarter, but Nvidia ( NVDA ) assumed no such shipments in its current forecast and said it was no longer shipping those products to the country.

Management said the outlook considered current US export controls, although it was still studying parts of the new rules announced on Monday, while demand elsewhere was expected to absorb the loss of China sales.

"Kress also provided confident answers around Commerce rules, citing that demand is far exceeding supply and that Nvidia ( NVDA ) is studying the rules around the chip delivery to other countries," said Christopher Brown, vice president of investments at Synovus, which holds Nvidia ( NVDA ) shares.

"We just need to understand that demand is not the same as legal ability to ship."

(Reporting by Shashwat Chauhan and Anhata Rooprai in Bengaluru, additional reporting by Avinash P and Noel Randewich; Editing by Joyjeet Das and Nick Zieminski)

data.title: Taiwan's Stock Pickers Are Walking Out to Bet Their Own Money
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fly On Wall Street News Commentary - Taiwan's benchmark stock index was up 62% this year, the best showing of any major equity gauge in the world, when Bloomberg reported on Oct. 16 that some of the island's professional fund managers and analysts are quitting their jobs to invest their own money. Strict rules keep them from trading the very stocks they pick for clients, and in a year when about one in ten stocks in the index has more than doubled, some have decided the trade-off is no longer worth it. Companies and funds mentioned in this article include: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited ( TSM ) [TSMC] , ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ( ASX ) [ASE] , United Microelectronics Corporation ( UMC ) [UMC] , iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF , The Taiwan Fund, Inc. ( TWN ) .

Watching From Behind the Locker

Taiwan does not ban personal investing outright, but its asset-management code of conduct bars staff from trading a locally listed stock or a linked derivative within seven business days before or after their firm's funds trade it, which in practice rules out personal stock-picking. Fund managers must also lock away their phones, laptops and smartwatches each morning until the market closes at 1:30 p.m. The phone rule was formalized in 2024 to deter insider trading, the Taipei Times reported in July, after six former fund managers from four firms were indicted for front-running trades through the accounts of relatives and friends.

Ken Tsai, 40, a fund manager who until July worked at a large Taiwanese asset manager that Bloomberg did not name, told Bloomberg he made a Taiwanese maker of AI-server data-transfer components his fund's largest holding in 2024. The stock rose more than fivefold in 2025 and about sixfold again this year, but he owned none of it personally. "It left me with a strong sense of relative deprivation," he said. He now works at a private investment firm in Taipei, which was also not named. Pay adds to the pull: Taiwan portfolio managers earn roughly US$124,000 to US$311,000 a year, well below Hong Kong base salaries, according to Bloomberg, citing headhunters and recruitment-firm data.

The private shops they are joining sit outside those rules. They register as private companies with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and do not need asset-management licenses from the Financial Supervisory Commission because they do not raise public money. Brokers told Bloomberg some of them now generate more than NT$10 billion in monthly trading volume, rivaling mid-sized asset managers.

The Rally Behind the Exits

Much of the rally traces back to the AI hardware supply chain. TSMC reported third-quarter revenue of NT$1.49 trillion (US$46.7 billion) on Oct. 15, up 50.9% from a year earlier, while net income jumped 68.7% and gross margin reached 66.4%. It guided fourth-quarter revenue from US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion.

Chip packaging and testing has ridden the same wave. ASE Technology ( ASX ) reported September net revenue of NT$88.1 billion, up 45.5% from a year earlier, and third-quarter revenue of NT$244.2 billion, up 44.8%.

Mature-node foundry UMC reported August sales up 30.71% from a year earlier, lifting year-to-date sales 14.66%. In its second-quarter report, the company guided for capacity utilization above 90% in the third quarter and said revenue from its 22/28nm business continues to set record highs.

CONTINUED... Read more market coverage at: flyonwallstreet.com

A Talent Squeeze, Not a Stampede

The numbers point to churn more than an exodus. Fewer than half of Taiwan's 20 largest local equity mutual funds have kept the same portfolio manager for more than three years, according to fund-data site MoneyDJ, and Bloomberg reported that applications for junior roles at some international firms have roughly halved this year. Yet the FSC said the industry's registered headcount actually rose to 4,729 in September from 4,581 at the end of 2025. Firms are responding: the largest foreign asset manager in Taiwan is offering cross-market analyst roles and office rotations to keep staff.

Regulators are paying attention. The FSC said on Oct. 15 it is gathering information and plans to review the rules, balancing market development against conflicts of interest and investor protection. One asset-management executive told Bloomberg there is no easy solution for now.

The Case for the Pros

At least one professionally managed fund has kept pace. The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ), a closed-end fund listed in New York, reported a 47.36% total return for its fiscal quarter ended May 31, against 26.12% for the TAIEX Total Return Index over the same period, with net asset value of US$116.90 a share at the end of that quarter.

Investors who prefer to own the whole market can use the iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF, which holds about US$11.9 billion in assets.

Last week was a reminder of how quickly the math can change. The TAIEX fell 4.6%, its first weekly decline in five weeks, as a technology selloff spread and TSMC CEO C.C. Wei warned of macroeconomic uncertainty and weak consumer demand, according to Trading Economics. In New York, TSMC's shares fell 8.98% from the Oct. 9 close to $412.61 on Oct. 16, ASE dropped 14.86% to $39.53, UMC slid 13.68% to $19.82, the iShares fund lost 7.04% to $106.26 and The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ) declined 8.78% to $94.18, according to Stock Analysis data. For the managers who just traded a salary for their own account, those swings now land on them.

data.title: Almost All Fed Officials See Need For Additional Rate Hikes, October Minutes Show
data.description:
03:29 PM EST, 11/18/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Almost all Federal Reserve officials agreed that interest rates must rise further to cool inflation, minutes from the central bank's October meeting showed Wednesday.

In a split vote on Oct. 28, the central bank's Federal Open Market Committee held its policy rate steady after a 25-basis-point hike in September. Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack preferred another quarter-percentage-point hike last month.

"Almost all participants judged that, under their baseline outlooks for inflation and the labor market, further action to raise the target range for the federal funds rate -- broadly consistent with the September Summary of Economic Projections -- would likely be appropriate, in order to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2% objective," the minutes showed.

A couple of participants at the October meeting said the Fed may need to raise its policy rate by more than 25 basis points at the next meeting if incoming inflation data were unfavorable, according to the minutes.

US inflation has remained above the Fed's 2% target for nearly six years. Most participants at the October FOMC meeting viewed price pressures to be broad based and expected inflation to remain elevated in the near term, the minutes showed.

"Many participants viewed the (artificial intelligence) buildout as a material source of inflation risk," according to the minutes.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller told CNBC Wednesday that the central bank may need to lift interest rates aggressively because inflation was "headed in the wrong direction."

The minutes showed a "stronger conviction in further hikes than (Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's post-meeting) press conference conveyed, with disagreement mainly over timing, a message we have received from Fed speakers since this meeting," said Vikram Rai, senior economist at TD Economics.

Fed Governor Michael Barr said Wednesday that raising interest rates will be appropriate to bring inflation down to the 2% target in a timely manner, joining other central bank officials who have recently leaned hawkish.

St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said on Tuesday that the FOMC will likely need to lift its policy rate "several" times before spring. Hammack has also pushed for policy tightening, though she recently said that it must be undertaken gradually.

Markets widely expect the central bank to raise its benchmark lending rate by 25 basis points next month, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

"A 25-basis-point December increase looks consistent with the broad consensus, but it is not assured, and a larger move is a conditional minority view," TD Economics' Rai said. "Broader inflation pass-through could require more restriction, while weaker AI investment and improving supply could limit it."

The Claude developer is expected to price its IPO later on Wednesday, and the shares will begin trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday.

"The combination of AI-driven enthusiasm and the lottery-like payoff profile typical of IPOs are likely to draw investors immediately. As one of the most concentrated pure-play exposures to AI, the stock is also likely to be highly volatile."

Interest in Anthropic options could exceed the interest in SpaceX options earlier this year, said Ophir Gottlieb, chief executive of Capital Market Laboratories, citing oversubscription that is pushing the company's valuation higher and could invite various positioning ahead of the deal, as well as the market backdrop.

"The AI trade is melting down," Gottlieb said. "Many feel it is overdone, while many others feel it's the popping of a bubble. Whenever there is such opposing views in a heated market, we get a lot of option positioning."

Options give holders the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell shares at a set price within a certain period. They offer investors a cheaper way to gain exposure to a stock and to express their views on both short-term price moves and longer-term positioning.

Anthropic's $64 billion IPO has drawn stronger early institutional demand than the offering of SpaceX, with the book six times oversubscribed last week, Reuters previously reported.

data.title: US judge rejects JPMorgan bid to dismiss lurid sexual harassment case
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 18 (Reuters) - JPMorgan Chase ( JPM ) failed on Wednesday to win the dismissal of a sexual harassment and discrimination lawsuit by former investment banker Chirayu Rana after accusing him of persuading his sister and a friend to lie for him.

US District Judge Lewis Kaplan in Manhattan also exhorted Rana, JPMorgan ( JPM ) and co-defendant Lorna Hajdini, a JPMorgan ( JPM ) executive, to press their claims and defenses through the court process, lamenting how the case "has been fought in part as a public relations battle."

JPMorgan ( JPM ) spokesperson Brian Marchiony declined to comment. Lawyers for Hajdini and Rana did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

In court papers, Rana accused Hajdini in graphic terms of sexual harassment, including by allegedly coercing him into sex and demanding submissiveness to advance his career. He also accused JPMorgan ( JPM ) of destroying his career by tolerating sexual coercion and racism, such as by doing nothing when colleagues called him "brown boy." Rana is of Nepalese descent.

JPMorgan ( JPM ) and Hajdini have denied Rana's claims, and Hajdini countersued him for defamation.

In seeking a dismissal, the largest US bank accused Rana of pressing his sister Chandani Rana and friend Allan Flott to lie about seeing some of Hajdini's alleged misconduct, including when she allegedly said "I own" Chirayu Rana. Chandani Rana later recanted her testimony.

Kaplan, a federal judge for 32 years and known for his no-nonsense handling of cases, said that "once the PR appeal of media attention is put to one side," he had no way to know whether Chandani Rana's original testimony or recantation was truthful.

He said such questions "normally are better put to juries than being made into subjects for time consuming and distracting mini-trials before judges on sanctions motions." Kaplan said the parties should focus on preparing for trial, or convincing him of their cases' merits.

The judge also said the case reminded him of the 1957 Oscar-nominated movie "Witness for the Prosecution," where a barrister played by Charles Laughton cross-examines a murder suspect's wife played by Marlene Dietrich: "The question is, Frau Helm, were you lying then, are you lying now, or are you not in fact a chronic and habitual LIAR?" ["Liar" is shouted.]

(Reporting by Jonathan Stempel in New York, Editing by Alexia Garamfalvi)

data.title: Liqid Announces Liqid as a Service to Break Through the AI Memory Wall with the Industry’s only Single-Tenant, Memory-Scaled Infrastructure Available as a Service Offering
data.description:
Dedicated, remotely accessed racks deliver faster time to first token, and initial testing delivered 5-7x more tokens per second from the same GPUs.

CHICAGO--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- At SC26, Liqid, the leader in software-defined memory and GPU pooling infrastructure, today announced Liqid as a Service, a fully managed, single-tenant AI infrastructure service for workloads that have outgrown a single server. Each Liqid as a Service node starts at 20 GPUs plus 10 TB of CXL memory but can scale to up to 30 GPUs and up to 160 TB of CXL memory to one server. Enterprises get room for large models, long context windows, and large datasets on dedicated infrastructure that Liqid operates for them.

AI performance now depends on memory as much as on compute. Models, agents, and datasets keep growing, but a typical AI server tops out at eight GPUs and a few terabytes of memory. Past that point, teams split work across servers, spill data to storage, or let GPUs recompute work they already finished. Each workaround costs speed, and many teams end up buying extra GPUs just to get more memory.

Liqid as a Service removes that ceiling. Liqid's fabric and Liqid Matrix software connect one host to pools of GPUs and CXL memory, so a single server can use far more memory than its own slots hold. In Liqid initial testing, the same GPUs produced 5-7x more tokens per second with this architecture.

“AI has hit a memory wall, and buying more GPUs that ultimately sit idle is the most expensive way over it,” said David Larson, President of Liqid. “Liqid as a Service gives enterprises the memory their models need, on infrastructure that belongs to them alone, without a capital project or a new datacenter. Liqid’s solutions are low power and air cooled by design, meaning the Liqid as a Service infrastructure foundation can circumvent longtail demand for new construction, liquid cooled datacenters and get customers producing tokens more quickly and cost-effectively.”

Designed for today’s datacenter power and cooling envelopes

Most datacenters were not built for today's largest AI racks. According to the Uptime Institute's 2026 Global Datacenter Survey, the typical rack draws about 11 kW, and 87 percent of datacenters have no rack at 50 kW or more.

Liqid as a Service fits inside those limits. A fully built node with 30 GPUs draws about 22 to 24 kW, is air cooled and occupies 14U of rack space. Liqid can run it in existing lights-out datacenters, colocation sites, and neocloud and service provider edge environments, with no liquid cooling and no new construction.

Private by design

Every deployment is single tenant. Each customer gets a whole or half rack that is never shared with another customer, and the security boundary sits at the customer's network edge. Liqid handles setup, hardware maintenance, and fault monitoring. Customers bring their own models and run their own stack.

Built for memory-bound work

Liqid as a Service targets workloads where the data no longer fits in one server and a faster answer carries real value. GPU options include NVIDIA H200 NVL, NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000, and AMD MI350P.

Liqid as a Service fits in environments where a faster answer pays off

Quantitative trading. Quant teams test ideas against years of tick-level market data. Holding that history in memory on one server lets researchers run more backtests in a day and move a signal into production while it still has an edge.

Fraud prevention. Fraud detection runs on graphs that link cards, accounts, devices, and merchants. Keeping the full graph in one server's memory lets banks score each transaction against every connection they have and flag suspicious activity before losses stack up.

Insurance underwriting. Underwriters price risk more accurately when their models draw on more history, more variables, and more scenarios. Larger memory lets carriers run risk models on full portfolios instead of samples and rerun scenarios as conditions change.

Pharma and life sciences. Discovery teams search for drug targets across genomic, protein, and screening data that runs to tens of terabytes. Working on whole datasets in memory, instead of slices, helps researchers find and rank promising targets sooner.

Liqid as a Service addresses workloads that hit the memory wall first

Long-context inference and AI agents. Every request and every agent builds a key-value (KV) cache of work already done. When that cache outgrows GPU and server memory, GPUs either recompute finished work or fetch it from storage that is about 100 times slower than memory. Liqid's pooled CXL memory gives the cache room to grow, so GPUs spend their time producing new tokens and one server can support more concurrent agents and longer contexts, including retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).

Large models on one server. A typical AI server tops out at eight GPUs. Liqid as a Service assigns up to 30 GPUs to a single host, so larger open models load and run on one system instead of being split across a network.

Graph analytics and HPC simulation. Graph databases can lose 30 to 50 percent of their performance with each server they are split across, according to Liqid testing. With up to 160 TB of memory behind one host, the whole graph or simulation stays in one place and runs at memory speed.

Proven technology

Liqid as a Service runs on the same pooled-memory technology that powers Micron's Abaco reference design that is deployed at Pacific Northwest National Laboratory, and has been proven to deliver 5-7x more tokens per second from the same GPUs.

Availability

SC26 attendees can learn more about Liqid as a Service by visiting booth 5214. Liqid as a Service general availability is planned for Q1 2027.

data.title: US STOCKS-Wall Street mixed after Nvidia earnings, Fed minutes
data.description:
(Updates to mid-afternoon trading)

* Indexes: Dow down 1.09%, S&P 500 down 0.27%, Nasdaq up 0.34%

* Fed minutes reveal commitment to hike rates prior to recent round of hot inflation data

* TJX jumps after forecasting upbeat annual sales

* Investors await Anthropic IPO pricing

By Stephen Culp and Utkarsh Hathi

Nov 18 (Reuters) - US stocks were mixed on Wednesday as investors digested Nvidia ( NVDA ) results ahead of Anthropic's initial public offering pricing, while weighing hawkish sentiment reflected in US Federal Reserve minutes.

After the three major US stock indexes wavered earlier in the session, by mid-afternoon the Nasdaq turned higher, the Dow was down, while the S&P 500 reversed its modest gains following release of the Fed minutes.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) quarterly results released late Tuesday beat analyst expectations, and the AI chipmaker forecast quarterly revenue above estimates. Even so, its shares were down 2.4% amid uncertainties caused by co-founder Jensen Huang's sudden departure last week.

The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor Index, which has handily outperformed the broader market this year, was off 0.7%, underscoring lofty expectations for the sector amid massive spending on AI infrastructure and potential risk associated with the nascent technology.

Anthropic's IPO is expected to price after the market closes on Wednesday. At the top of its $70 to $78 range, the offering would raise about $64.4 billion and value the company at about $1.4 trillion.

Other chipmakers were mixed. Intel ( INTC ) was off 1.8%, Micron was down 2%, but Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) rose 3.2%.

"There's been a lot of dark clouds of uncertainty over technology, chip stocks and AI in general," said Ryan Detrick, chief market strategist at Carson Group in Omaha. "It's important to remember the market's not totally falling apart here. It clearly is top-heavy with tech, but there are other groups that are actually doing pretty well under the surface."

Target ( TGT ) jumped 6.3% after the discount retailer provided an upbeat holiday outlook. Results from its larger rival Walmart are expected on Thursday.

TJX surged 10.6% after forecasting upbeat annual sales, banking on strong demand ahead of the holiday shopping season.

Take-Two Interactive shares rose 7.7% ahead of the rollout of its Grand Theft Auto VI video game.

On the sector level, consumer discretionary was a clear outperformer, with a boost from a 3.8% gain in Amazon ( AMZN ) shares.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 555.11 points, or 1.09%, to 50,204.31, the S&P 500 lost 19.48 points, or 0.27%, to 7,321.05 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 82.36 points, or 0.34%, to 24,410.75.

FOCUS ON THE FED

Minutes from the Fed's October policy meeting showed the central bank remained focused on inflation risks, recognizing the need for further rate hikes if the economy progresses as expected. A few policymakers argued the case for a 50-basis-point rate hike "if incoming inflation data were unfavorable."

Consumer and producer price data released after the October meeting showed hotter-than-expected price growth.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller took a hawkish stance on Wednesday, saying the central bank needs to be more aggressive in responding to inflation. This follows John Williams' comments on Tuesday, in which the New York Fed president said that while he favors tighter monetary policy, there was no need for "dramatic action."

Financial markets are pricing in a 94.7% probability of a 25-basis-point interest rate hike at the conclusion of the Fed's December meeting, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

Housing data released on Wednesday showed mortgage rates climbing, building permits faltering, and pending home sales dropping to a record low.

On the Nasdaq, 2,345 stocks rose and 2,330 fell as advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.01-to-1 ratio.

The S&P 500 posted 4 new 52-week highs and 8 new lows, while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 28 new highs and 369 new lows.

data.title: Nissan uses Mexico to prep for potential China challenge in US
data.description:
Nov 18 (Reuters) - As head of Nissan's ( NSANF ) US business, Christian Meunier doesn't need to imagine what might happen if fast-rising Chinese car brands one day crack the American market. He's already been confronting that battle south of the border, in Mexico.

Meunier, chairman of Nissan Americas, oversees the Japanese automaker's operations across the Western Hemisphere. He has been fending off an influx of Chinese brands in Mexico, where Nissan ( NSANF ) has been the top-selling car company for many years.

Meunier said his team is working on reducing costs to be able to match Chinese competitors by shortening the vehicle-development process, reducing supply chain costs and other tactics. 

"Our cost base today in [the US] is not competitive. It's not strong enough," Meunier said at a conference in Detroit hosted by MEMA, The Vehicle Suppliers Association. 

REVIVING US BUSINESS A FOCUS

Exports of Chinese cars have surged over the past three years, sending global automakers scrambling to compete with vehicles that often are priced 30% cheaper than domestic models. 

For now, Meunier's main focus is revitalizing the Nissan brand in the US, where the automaker's market share sank by one-third over a decade through last year. It has been rebounding but, at around 6%, remains well below its peak. 

Nissan ( NSANF ) is planning a blitz of new models to bring back customers. Up first is a hybrid version of its top seller, the Rogue compact SUV, which began arriving at showrooms in recent weeks. 

Later in the decade, Nissan ( NSANF ) plans to roll out several rugged SUVs built on ​a truck-like frame, including the reintroduction of the Xterra, which was sold in ​the US from ⁠the 1990s to the mid-2010s.

For now, Meunier isn't worried about Chinese car brands in the US, where a combination of tariffs and a ban on Chinese software has effectively blocked their entry. But he figures they could show up within the next five or 10 years. 

"We need to be ready," he said at a media briefing Tuesday. 

MEXICO AN 'EXPERIMENT' TO PREP FOR CHINESE RIVALS IN US

There is more urgency in Mexico, where Chinese brands have been importing cars to grab a 10% market share in a short period, according to research firm AutoForecast Solutions. A tariff that took effect early this year limits the Chinese companies' ability to undercut the market on price. 

Meunier said Nissan ( NSANF ) has "a two-year window" before the Chinese companies begin making cars in Mexico, avoiding levies. He wants to get Nissan's ( NSANF ) costs down during that period through automation and simpler engineering. 

He sees that effort in Mexico as a test run for eventually competing against Chinese rivals in the US market.

"Mexico is going to be a really good ground for us to experiment and to learn" how to match the Chinese on cost, he said.

(Reporting by Mike Colias in Detroit; editing by Diane Craft)

data.title: Fed's Barr says rate rises likely lie ahead for economy

NEW YORK, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr said Wednesday he's likely to be on board with tighter monetary policy in an economy still beset by inflation pressures.

"If the economy evolves as I currently forecast, I expect it will be appropriate to raise rates further," Barr said in the text of remarks prepared for delivery before a conference at the New York Fed.

"Inflation is too high, making it hard for American families to make ends meet. Many families are struggling" under the weight of price pressures, Barr said.

The official also noted that while inflation is an issue, the economy is otherwise doing well. "The economy is strong, with low unemployment, solid consumer spending, and robust business investment," Barr said.

The Fed's interest-rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee is scheduled to meet on December 8 and 9. It is widely expected to raise its current federal funds target rate range by a quarter percentage point, to between 4% and 4.25%.

data.title: Fed policymakers focused on inflation risks in October, with some seeing need for bigger rate hike
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Federal Reserve officials saw a growing risk last month that they might need to intensify their efforts to control inflation, even as they agreed to keep interest rates steady for the moment, the minutes of their October 27-28 meeting showed on Wednesday.

"Almost all" policymakers agreed that further rate hikes would be needed if the economy evolved as they expected, the minutes said, while a few said inflation could prove more persistent and require "a shift to a more restrictive policy stance" than currently expected.

"A couple" of them went further and argued that the Fed might have to resort to a half-percentage-point increase "if incoming inflation data were unfavorable," a benchmark met in recent releases that showed prices rising faster than anticipated.

Among those who supported keeping the policy rate steady in the 3.75%-4.00% range in October, "a few ... indicated that they viewed the decision as a close call," and joined a larger group in urging that the Fed be clear that "the decision to maintain the target range did not reflect a weakening" of the commitment to hit the US central bank's 2% inflation target.

At the end of the two-day session, only Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented in favor of lifting the policy rate by a quarter of a percentage point.  

But the debate highlighted a growing sense at the Fed that inflation will not ease enough on its own for the target to be reached quickly enough. Among those supporting a rate-hike pause, the hope is that coming information will make clearer whether inflation can fall without tighter policy.

Prices have been increasing at more than a 3% annual rate, and there has been little improvement in recent months.

Last month's meeting also set the stage for a potentially intense debate at the December 8-9 session over the need for a larger rate hike, or at least tougher language about the extent and pace of rate hikes to come, an argument laid out by Fed Governor Christopher Waller in comments to CNBC on Wednesday.

The Trump administration has argued that elevated inflation is just temporary and the Fed should ignore it.

Inflation has been stronger than expected since the Fed's last meeting, and investors anticipate that the central bank will deliver a quarter-percentage-point rate increase at its meeting next month.

The October meeting also saw the beginnings of a more detailed discussion about the impact of artificial intelligence, including discussion of the risks of over-investment in the technology as well as the possible benefits it could bring in the form of rising productivity.

(Reporting by Howard Schneider; Editing by Paul Simao)
